text:
Marta: Hi everyone, first morning on Fedora 38. Following the Linux bootstrap but running into a weird mix: asdf install golang 1.20.5 fails with `go: cannot find C compiler` even though gcc is present. Also VS Code installed as a flatpak doesn't pick up my zsh login shell, so `code` launched from the Activities menu doesn't see my asdf shims. Anyone on Fedora hit this?

Jules: Welcome Marta! :wave: Two quick things: 1) Flatpak apps run in sandbox and won't see your host PATH unless you use the Flatpak portal or install VS Code from RPM. 2) For the go build error, what's the output of `gcc --version` and `which cc`?

Marta: `gcc --version` -> gcc (GCC) 13.2.1, `which cc` -> /usr/bin/cc. The asdf log shows `exec: "cc": executable file not found in $PATH` inside the build step. Feels like the build sandbox can't see /usr/bin.

IT: Fedora packs some build tools into `@development` group. Try `sudo dnf groupinstall "Development Tools"` and also `sudo dnf install glibc-devel`. For asdf-go build, the plugin spawns a subshell; make sure you don't have a sanitized PATH in your dotfiles e.g., setting PATH only in graphical login file.

Jules: About Flatpak VS Code, easiest is to install `code` via RPM from our devex package repo or use `flatpak run --command=code com.visualstudio.code` from a terminal that has the right env forwarded. There's also `flatpak override --user --env=PATH=$PATH com.visualstudio.code` but that can be brittle. We recommend RPM for dev.

Marta: Installed the dev tools and glibc-devel, re-ran `asdf install golang 1.20.5` and the C compiler error went away. VS Code note: I installed the RPM and now the GUI picks up `~/.asdf/shims` when launched. Two follow-ups: 1) Podman replacing Docker — my docker-compose files fail with `permission denied` when podman-compose runs; 2) gpg commit signing was working with Seahorse but now VS Code commits show unsigned.

IT: For podman and volumes, SELinux context on Fedora can cause permission denied. Try `podman run --rm -v $(pwd):/work:Z ...` (the :Z adds the correct SELinux relabel). Alternatively set `chcon -R -t container_file_t ./` on your project directory. For docker-compat, we recommend `podman-docker` package which provides /usr/bin/docker shim.

Jules: For gpg signing in VS Code, make sure the code process can see the GPG agent socket. If you use GNOME keyring/Seahorse, export `GPG_AGENT_INFO` or configure `gpg --card-status` accordingly. A simpler route: use `git config --global gpg.program gpg` and ensure `gpg --list-secret-keys` shows your key in the env where VS Code runs. After changing flatpak -> rpm you likely fixed the socket visibility issue.

Marta: Podman fix worked with `:Z` mount. For signing, `gpg --list-secret-keys` was empty in the GUI environment; after switching to RPM VS Code the key appears and commits are signed. Final tiny Q: direnv complains about `ALLOW_UNKNOWN` when my dotfiles add a private env file. Any team policy on secrets in envrc?

IT: Don't commit secrets. Use direnv to load from 1Password (`op`) or use `direnv` + `envrc` that sources a local `secrets.env` which is in .gitignore. For policy, we ask you to keep secrets out of git — if you accidentally committed something, open a ticket with `@it` for help with credential rotation.

Marta: Great — switched VS Code to RPM, fixed podman SELinux relabel, installed dev tools, and added a `SETUP.Fedora.md` to my dotfiles describing the Flatpak caveat and SELinux tip. Thanks all!

Devex Bot: Welcome Marta! Short checklist for Fedora: dnf groupinstall "Development Tools", install glibc-devel, prefer RPM VS Code for shell integration, use `podman-docker` shim or `:Z` mounts for SELinux, and commit `asdf/.tool-versions` to your dotfiles. See https://redwood.ai/devex/linux for the canonical guide.
